repositories.readme: # Ghidra Software Reverse Engineering Framework Ghidra is a software reverse engineering (SRE) framework created and maintained by the [National Security Agency][nsa] Research Directorate. This framework includes a suite of full-featured, high-end software analysis tools that enable users to analyze compiled code on a variety of platforms including Windows, macOS, and Linux. Capabilities include disassembly, assembly, decompilation, graphing, and scripting, along with hundreds of other features. Ghidra supports a wide variety of processor instruction sets and executable formats and can be run in both user-interactive and automated modes. Users may also develop their own Ghidra extension components and/or scripts using Java or Python. In support of NSA's Cybersecurity mission, Ghidra was built to solve scaling and teaming problems on complex SRE efforts, and to provide a customizable and extensible SRE research platform. NSA has applied Ghidra SRE capabilities to a variety of problems that involve analyzing malicious code and generating deep insights for SRE analysts who seek a better understanding of potential vulnerabilities in networks and systems. If you are a U.S. citizen interested in projects like this, to develop Ghidra and other cybersecurity tools for NSA to help protect our nation and its allies, consider applying for a [career with us][career]. ## Security Warning **WARNING:** There are known security vulnerabilities within certain versions of Ghidra. Before proceeding, please read through Ghidra's [Security Advisories][security] for a better understanding of how you might be impacted. ## Install To install an official pre-built multi-platform Ghidra release: * Install [JDK 25 64-bit][jdk] * Download a Ghidra [release file][releases] - **NOTE:** The official multi-platform release file is named `ghidra___.zip` which can be found under the "Assets" drop-down. Downloading either of the files named "Source Code" is not correct for this step. * Extract the Ghidra release file - **NOTE:** Do not extract on top of an existing installation * Launch Ghidra: `./ghidraRun` (`ghidraRun.bat` for Windows) - or launch [PyGhidra][pyghidra]: `./support/pyghidraRun` (`support\pyghidraRun.bat` for Windows) For additional information and troubleshooting tips about installing and running a Ghidra release, please refer to the [Getting Started][gettingstarted] document which can be found at the root of a Ghidra installation directory. ## Build [![Build Ghidra][build-ghidra-badge]][build-ghidra-action] To create the latest development build for your platform from this source repository: ##### Install build tools: * [JDK 25 64-bit][jdk] * [Gradle 9.1.0+][gradle] (or provided Gradle wrapper if Internet connection is available) * [Python3][python3] (version 3.9 to 3.15) with bundled pip * GCC or Clang, and make (Linux/macOS-only) * [Microsoft Visual Studio][vs] 2017+ or [Microsoft C++ Build Tools][vcbuildtools] with the following components installed (Windows-only): - MSVC - Windows SDK - C++ ATL ##### Download and extract the source: [Download from GitHub][master] ``` unzip ghidra-master cd ghidra-master ``` **NOTE:** Instead of downloading the compressed source, you may instead want to clone the GitHub repository: `git clone https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra.git` ##### Download additional build dependencies into source repository: **NOTE:** If an Internet connection is available and you did not install Gradle, the `./gradlew` (or `gradlew.bat`) command may be used in place of the `gradle` command in the following instructions. ``` gradle -I gradle/support/fetchDependencies.gradle ``` ##### Create development build: ``` gradle buildGhidra ``` The compressed development build will be located at `build/dist/`. For more detailed information on building Ghidra, please read the [Developer's Guide][devguide]. For issues building, please check the [Known Issues][known-issues] section for possible solutions. ## Develop ### User Scripts and Extensions Ghidra installations support users writing custom scripts and extensions via the *GhidraDev* plugin for Eclipse. The plugin and its corresponding instructions can be found within a Ghidra release at `Extensions/Eclipse/GhidraDev/` or at [this link][ghidradev]. Alternatively, Visual Studio Code may be used to edit scripts by clicking the Visual Studio Code icon in the Script Manager. Fully-featured Visual Studio Code projects can be created from a Ghidra CodeBrowser window at _Tools -> Create VSCode Module project_. **NOTE:** Both the *GhidraDev* plugin for Eclipse and Visual Studio Code integrations only support developing against fully built Ghidra installations which can be downloaded from the [Releases][releases] page. ### Advanced Development To develop the Ghidra tool itself, it is highly recommended to use Eclipse, which the Ghidra development process has been highly customized for. ##### Install build and development tools: * Follow the above [build instructions](#build) so the build completes without errors * Install [Eclipse IDE for Java Developers][eclipse] ##### Prepare the development environment: ``` gradle prepdev eclipse buildNatives ``` ##### Import Ghidra projects into Eclipse: * *File* -> *Import...* * *General* | *Existing Projects into Workspace* * Select root directory to be your downloaded or cloned ghidra source repository * Check *Search for nested projects* * Click *Finish* When Eclipse finishes building the projects, Ghidra can be launched and debugged with the provided **Ghidra** Eclipse *run configuration*. For more detailed information on developing Ghidra, please read the [Developer's Guide][devguide]. ## Contribute If you would like to contribute bug fixes, improvements, and new features back to Ghidra, please take a look at our [Contributor's Guide][contrib] to see how you can participate in this open source project. [build-ghidra-action]: https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/actions/workflows/build-ghidra.yml [build-ghidra-badge]: https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/actions/workflows/build-ghidra.yml/badge.svg [nsa]: https://www.nsa.gov [contrib]: CONTRIBUTING.md [devguide]: DevGuide.md [gettingstarted]: GhidraDocs/GettingStarted.md [known-issues]: DevGuide.md#known-issues [career]: https://www.intelligencecareers.gov/nsa [releases]: https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/releases [jdk]: https://adoptium.net/temurin/releases [gradle]: https://gradle.org/releases/ [python3]: https://www.python.org/downloads/ [vs]: https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/vs/community/ [vcbuildtools]: https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/ [eclipse]: https://www.eclipse.org/downloads/packages/ [master]: https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/archive/refs/heads/master.zip [security]: https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/security/advisories [ghidradev]: GhidraBuild/EclipsePlugins/GhidraDev/GhidraDevPlugin/README.md [pyghidra]: Ghidra/Features/PyGhidra/README.md

repositories.name: jiangshan-map
repositories.description: 江山时序 · 中国历史交互地图时间轴 (403 BCE – Present) | Interactive Historical Atlas of China across 18 dynasties, 164 territory snapshots, ancient-to-modern place genealogy & classical poetry routes
repositories.readme:
# Chronicles of the Realm · 江山时序

English · 简体中文 (Chinese)

**An Interactive Historical Atlas of China from the Warring States (403 BCE) to the Present — Scrub Through Time, Trace Ancient Cities, and Walk in the Footsteps of History** [**Play Live Demo (English UI) → https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en**](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en) *The story behind it (in Chinese): [From textbook maps to 1k GitHub stars](https://deanchen.me/history/atlas/2026/10/25/jiangshan-map-story.html)*

--- ## Why It's Fun to Explore Have you ever wondered while reading Chinese history or classical poetry: - *"Where exactly on today's map are Jiankang (the Six Dynasties capital), Huangzhou (where Su Dongpo composed the Red Cliffs Rhapsody in exile), Languan Pass in the Qinling Mountains (where Han Yu halted his horse in the snow), or Zhuxianzhen (Yue Fei's northern campaign frontier)?"* - *"How many names did Chang'an hold across two millennia, and what pivotal events unfolded on that soil?"* - *"How did the realm evolve step by step—from the Partition of Jin and the Seven Warring States at the opening of Sima Guang's Zizhi Tongjian (403 BCE), Qin's unification campaigns, Emperor Wu of Han opening the Hexi Corridor, High Tang's Four Garrisons of Anxi, and Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan jurisdiction over Tibet, to Zeng Jize's recovery of Ili (1881 CE) and the 20th-century shift from the 'Begonia Leaf' (秋海棠) map to the 'Rooster' (雄鸡) map?"* **Chronicles of the Realm (`jiangshan-map`)** brings together **2,400+ years** of Chinese history across **18 historical periods** into a single interactive parchment atlas—featuring **multi-stage territorial and prefecture snapshots**, **ancient cities**, **strategic mountain passes**, **poetic and battlefield landmarks**, **chronological milestones**, and **reigning monarchs & imperial eras**. No heavy print atlases required—just drag the timeline and click any city to travel through space and time. --- ### Feature 1: Scrub the Timeline to Watch Realms Rise & Fall, Track Monarchs, and Compare Ancient & Modern Borders - **Multi-Polity Confrontations on a Single Canvas**: From the Seven Warring States (Qin, Chu, Qi, Yan, Zhao, Wei, Han) alongside Zhou, Yue, Ba-Shu, Zhongshan, and Yiqu, to the Three Kingdoms warlords (Yuan Shao, Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Sun Quan, Gongsun's Liaodong), Northern & Southern Dynasties, Five Dynasties & Ten Kingdoms, and Song, Liao, Western Xia, Dali, Jin, and the Mongols—all rendered side-by-side in high-contrast traditional parchment hues. Hover over any polity in the bottom-left legend to highlight its territory, or click to zoom straight to it. - **Multi-Stage Territorial Evolution & Dashed "Ghost Boundary Diffs"**: At every major territorial milestone—such as Qin's conquest of Ba-Shu (316 BCE), Yan General Qin Kai's expansion into Liaodong (300 BCE), Ma Yuan's bronze pillars in Jiaozhi (43 CE), Sima Yi's campaign in Liaodong (238 CE), Li Jing's conquest of Tuyuhun (635 CE), the Four Garrisons of Anxi & Wang Xuance's campaign in Central India (648 CE), Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan rule over Tibet (1288 CE), Ming's Hami & Seven Guards West of Jiayuguan (1404 CE), the 1881 Treaty of Saint Petersburg recovering Ili, the 1898 foreign leased territories, the 1945 retrocession of Taiwan, and the 1946 transition from the **"Begonia Leaf" (秋海棠)** map to the **"Rooster" (雄鸡)** map—click any milestone or phase dot to switch maps and reveal the previous phase's dashed vermilion **Ghost Boundary Diff** so territorial gains and losses are immediately visible. - **Inline Reigning Monarch & Imperial Era Display**: The timeline dynamically displays the reigning monarch (temple/posthumous title + personal name + reign span, e.g., `Emperor Wu of Han · Liu Che`, `Emperor Taizong of Tang · Li Shimin`, `Emperor Shengzu of Qing · Xuanye`) alongside the exact imperial era year. - **Ancient Prefecture Hover Inspection & Modern X-Ray Lens**: First-level administrative divisions (Commanderies, Circuits, Routes, and Provinces) are rendered with deduplicated **Parchment Casing** borders. Zoom in and hover over any prefecture (e.g., Ming `Yingtian Prefecture` or Three Kingdoms `Jingzhou`) to inspect its jurisdiction and modern provincial equivalents, or toggle the **X-Ray Lens** to project modern provincial boundaries directly over the historical map. - **Dynamic River Courses, Ancient Lakes & Grand Engineering Works**: As you scrub through time, historical shifts of the Yellow River, expanding and shrinking ancient lakes (*Yunmeng Marsh*, *Lop Nur / Puchanghai*), Warring States/Qin/Han/Ming Great Walls, Sui-Tang & Grand Canals, the Silk Road, and Zheng He's maritime routes evolve in lockstep with each era. > [Try It Live: Ming Dynasty Yongle 13 (1415 CE) · Two Capitals, Thirteen Provinces & "Yingtian Prefecture" Inspection →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1415&zoom=1.75¢er=115.8,33.2&hover=Yingtian%20Prefecture&lang=en) ![Ming Dynasty 1415 CE · Yingtian Prefecture Hover Preview](assets/preview_1415_ming_yingtian_en.webp) --- ### Feature 2: Click Any Ancient City or Strategic Pass to Uncover 2,400 Years of History (`Trace Place`) **Click any ancient city or mountain pass** on the map (or double-click anywhere on the canvas) to open its **Trace Place** genealogy card: - **Bilingual City Lore Banner & 2,400-Year Administrative Genealogy**: At the top of the card, read a curated **poetic epigraph and historical biography** for the city; below, trace how its name and administrative jurisdiction evolved across all 18 historical eras—from Warring States and Qin commanderies, Han regional inspectorates, Tang circuits, and Song routes to Yuan/Ming/Qing provinces and modern municipalities—complete with `Imperial Capital` badges and dynastic seat remarks. - **Site-Specific Landmark Events**: Beneath each dynasty row, inspect major historical events that took place right on that spot (e.g., *Shang Yang's Reforms* and *Qin's Unification* at Xianyang, *Guan Yu Flooding the Seven Armies* at Fancheng, the *Xuanwu Gate Incident* at Chang'an, or *Yue Fei's Martyrdom* at Lin'an). Click the **`Key Events`** pill in the top-right of the card to filter for dynasties with major events, and click any event to time-travel straight to that year! - **Strategic Mountain Passes & Poetic / Battlefield Landmarks**: Explore famous mountain passes—including *Hangu Pass*, *Tongguan*, *Jianmen Pass*, *Yanmen Pass*, *Yumen Pass*, *Yangguan*, and *Shanhai Pass*—rendered with traditional *Hanque* gatehouse icons and strategic terrain notes, alongside famous battlefields and literary landmarks such as *Red Cliffs (Chibi)*, *Gaixia*, *Wuzhang Plains*, *Orchid Pavilion (Lanting)*, *Yueyang Tower*, *Pavilion of Prince Teng*, *Languan Pass*, *Loulan*, *Lop Nur*, and *Issyk-Kul*. > [Try It Live: High Tang Kaiyuan 29 (741 CE) · Open Chang'an's 2,400-Year Genealogy Card →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=741&place=Chang'an&lang=en) ![High Tang 741 CE · Chang'an Trace Place & Key Events](assets/preview_741_tang_trace_en.webp) --- ### Feature 3: Person Chronicles — Trace Any Historical Figure Across Time & Space Click the top-left **Universal Search Box** (with a rotatable `e.g.` figure preview and quick-search chips, or type any monarch, general, statesman, monk, or poet such as `Cao Cao`, `Huo Qubing`, `Sima Qian`, `Yue Fei`, or `Zheng He`) to open **Person Chronicle (`点人溯事`)**, plotting every milestone of their life with delicate cartographic hairline arcs and directional ticks across changing dynastic borders: - **Qin Shi Huang's Unification Campaigns (238–221 BCE)**: From suppressing the rebellion at Xianyang and Wang Jian's attack on Ye, to the fall of Han, Zhao, Yan, Wei, Chu, and Dai, culminating in the surrender of Qi at Linzi—as you advance stop by stop, watch the six rival kingdoms merge into the Qin Empire right on the map! - **Zhang Qian's Mission to the Western Regions (138–126 BCE)**: Depart Chang'an, endure over a decade of Xiongnu captivity without surrendering the Han imperial staff, and blaze the trail to Dayuan (Fergana), Kangju, and the Greater Yuezhi. - **Zhuge Liang's Emergence & Northern Expeditions (207–234 CE)**: From the Three Visits at Longzhong and the alliance at Chaisang before Red Cliffs, to entering Shu, the White Emperor City entrustment, the Southern Campaign across the Lu River, Hanzhong's *Memorial on Deploying the Troops*, Mount Qi, and the autumn winds of Wuzhang Plains. - **Xuanzang's Pilgrimage to India (627–645 CE)**: Slip past Yumen Pass alone across the Moheyan Desert, scale the icy Bedel Pass, cross the Indus, study at Nalanda Monastery, and debate at Kanyakubja (Kanauj) before returning to Chang'an. - **Li Bai's Grand Travels Across Tang China (701–762 CE)**: From Suyab and boyhood in Shu, sailing out through the Three Gorges at twenty-four, scattering gold in Yangzhou, serving in the Hanlin Academy at Chang'an, meeting Du Fu in Luoyang, receiving amnesty at White Emperor City, to his final years at Dangtu. - **Su Shi's Literary Exile Across Song China (1056–1101 CE)**: From leaving Meishan for the capital Kaifeng and gazing at the moon in Mizhou, to composing the *Red Cliffs Rhapsody* in Huangzhou exile, Huizhou, and crossing the sea to Danzhou on Hainan Island. - **Wang Yangming's Unity of Knowledge & Action (1472–1529 CE)**: From birth in Yuyao and imprisonment in Beijing, to his enlightenment at Longchang in Guizhou, pacifying bandits in Southern Ganzhou, capturing the rebel Prince of Ning in 35 days, teaching at the Tianquan Bridge in Shaoxing, and his final words *"This mind is bright and clear; what more is there to say?"* at Nan'an. Each time you step to the next event (`‹ / ›`, `← / →`, or `Space` to auto-play), **the timeline year, reigning monarch, imperial era, and dynastic territories evolve in sync with their footsteps**, highlighting the active transition arc alongside bilingual primary-source excerpts and poems written at that exact site. > [Try It Live: Follow Su Dongpo's Exile to Mizhou & Huangzhou (1075–1082 CE) →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=sushi&lang=en) ![Person Chronicle · Su Shi's Life & Exile Route](assets/preview_journey_sushi_en.webp) --- ### Feature 4: Easter Egg · Map Pinpoint Challenge — What Imperial Court Rank Would You Earn? Think you know Chinese historical geography? Click **`Quiz ›`** in the corner of the **Universal Search Box** guide bar (or type `quiz` for **`Map Pinpoint · Ancient Place Quiz`**): - **Dynastic Historical Clues + Blind Map Pinpointing**: City labels are hidden while the prompt asks you to locate an ancient city across a 10-round progressive difficulty deck—accompanied by **dynastic historical clues** (without spoiling the modern city name). Drop your pin to preview and adjust, click the on-pin **`✓ Confirm`** button to lock in your answer with concentric distance score rings, and earn points based on great-circle distance to the true coordinates! - Complete 10 rounds to receive a traditional imperial cartographic title such as **Grand Historian & Master Cartographer (太史令 · 舆图大家)**, **Director of the Bureau of Operations (职方郎中)**, or **Prefectural Retainer (州郡从事)**. > [Try It Live: Western Han Emperor Wu, Yuanshou 2 (121 BCE) · Start the Map Pinpoint Challenge →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-121&quiz=locate&lang=en) ![Western Han 121 BCE · Map Pinpoint Challenge Preview](assets/preview_quiz_challenge_en.webp) --- ## Keyboard Shortcuts & Shareable Deep Links ### Keyboard Shortcuts | Key / Action | Effect | | :--- | :--- | | **`/`** or **`Cmd/Ctrl + K`** | Focus the **Universal Search Box**: search **historical figures** (`Qin Shi Huang`/`Zhang Qian`/`Su Shi`), **ancient & modern cities** (`Xianyang`/`Chang'an`/`Luoyang`/`Kaifeng`), **reigning monarchs** (`Emperor Wu of Han`/`Taizong of Tang`/`Liu Che`/`Li Shimin`), **imperial eras** (`Zhenguan`/`Yongle`/`Kangxi`), **poetic & battlefield landmarks** (`Red Cliffs`/`Wuzhang Plains`/`Languan`/`Lanting`), **mountain passes** (`Hangu Pass`/`Jianmen Pass`/`Yumen Pass`), **historical events**, or the **Ancient Place Quiz** | | **`←` / `→`** or bottom **`‹ / ›`** | Jump to the previous / next historical phase, milestone event, or person event stop (hold `Shift + ← / →` to step by `10` years) | | **`Space`** | Auto-play / pause timeline evolution (or auto-advance stops in Person Chronicle mode) | | **`Esc`** | Close active popups/cards, clear search highlights, or exit custom multi-stop routes | | **`Single-click city` / `Double-click map`** | Open the 18-era **Trace Place & Key Events** genealogy card for that location | | **`Hover / Click legend swatch`** | Hover to isolate & highlight that polity's territory; click to auto-zoom to its bounding box | ### Shareable Deep Links Append query parameters to share any historical moment, battle, city genealogy, or multi-stop route: - **Jump to a specific year or territorial shift**: [`?year=-403&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-403&lang=en) (403 BCE · Partition of Jin) / [`?year=-121&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-121&lang=en) (121 BCE · Huo Qubing opens the Hexi Corridor) / [`?year=648&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=648&lang=en) (648 CE · Four Garrisons of Anxi & Wang Xuance in India) / [`?year=1288&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1288&lang=en) (1288 CE · Yuan Xuanzhengyuan over Tibet) / [`?year=1881&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1881&lang=en) (1881 CE · Zeng Jize recovers Ili) / [`?year=1945&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1945&lang=en) (1945 CE · Retrocession of Taiwan) - **Pinpoint a famous battle**: [`?year=-260&place=长平&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-260&place=长平&lang=en) (Battle of Changping) / [`?year=208&place=赤壁&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=208&place=赤壁&lang=en) (Battle of Red Cliffs) / [`?year=383&place=淝水&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=383&place=淝水&lang=en) (Battle of Fei River) - **Inspect a city's 2,400-year genealogy**: [`?year=741&place=长安&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=741&place=长安&lang=en) (Chang'an / Xi'an) / [`?year=1415&place=应天府&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1415&place=应天府&lang=en) (Jiankang / Yingtian / Nanjing) / [`?year=819&place=蓝关&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=819&place=蓝关&lang=en) (Han Yu at Languan Pass) - **Plot a custom poetic or campaign route**: [`?year=763&place=剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=763&place=剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳&lang=en) (Du Fu's 763 CE homeward route) / [`?year=1079,1080,1094,1097&place=湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1079,1080,1094,1097&place=湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州&lang=en) (Su Shi's multi-year exile route across Huzhou, Huangzhou, Huizhou, and Danzhou) - **Open a person's spatio-temporal chronicle**: [`?person=qinshihuang&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=qinshihuang&lang=en) (Qin Shi Huang) / [`?person=zhangqian&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=zhangqian&lang=en) (Zhang Qian) / [`?person=zhugeliang&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=zhugeliang&lang=en) (Zhuge Liang) / [`?person=xuanzang&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=xuanzang&lang=en) (Xuanzang) / [`?person=libai&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=libai&lang=en) (Li Bai) / [`?person=sushi&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=sushi&lang=en) (Su Shi) / [`?person=wangyangming&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=wangyangming&lang=en) (Wang Yangming) - **Start a quiz round**: [`?year=-121&quiz=locate&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-121&quiz=locate&lang=en) (Map Pinpoint Challenge) - **Switch UI language**: [`?lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en) (English) / [`?lang=zh-tw`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=zh-tw) (Traditional Chinese) / [`/`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/) (Simplified Chinese) ### Embed in Your Page Put any view of the atlas into a blog post, Notion page, or course site: 1. Open the atlas and set up the view you want (a year, a regime profile, a place card, or a person's trajectory). The address bar always mirrors what you see. 2. Copy the URL and add `&embed=1`. 3. Paste it into an ` ``` The embedded map hides the site chrome and keeps only the map, a compact timeline, a title chip, an "Open in Jiangshan Atlas ↗" link, and a note that historical borders are approximate. Readers click once to start panning and zooming, so scrolling your page never gets stuck on the map. | Parameter | Effect | |---|---| | `embed=1` | Turn on embed mode (required) | | `year`, `polity`, `person`, `stop`, `trace`, `lang` | Same as the share links above | | `from=1072&to=1126` | Limit the timeline to this range; the timeline zooms to show only it | | `lock=1` | Freeze the map at `year` and hide the timeline | | `autoplay=1` | Play a person's trajectory stop by stop (with `person`), or play the timeline | WeChat Official Accounts, Zhihu, and Xiaohongshu do not allow iframes; share the plain link there instead. --- ## AI Agent, MCP & LLM Integration **Chronicles of the Realm** works out of the box as a **historical-geography visualization engine for LLMs, MCP Clients, and AI Agents**. Models **never need to guess latitude/longitude coordinates**—simply extract two semantic parameters from a poem or historical text, **`year`** and **`place`**, and the atlas automatically resolves ancient/modern place names, centers the camera, renders dynastic borders and multi-stop trajectories, and opens the **Trace Place** genealogy card: - **Machine-Readable Specification**: [`llms.txt`](llms.txt) - **Zero-Dependency Local MCP Server (`stdio`)**: [`scripts/mcp_server.js`](scripts/mcp_server.js) — add to Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, or Gemini CLI `mcpServers`: ```json { "mcpServers": { "jiangshan-atlas": { "command": "node", "args": ["/absolute/path/to/jiangshan-map/scripts/mcp_server.js"] } } } ``` Exposes 3 native MCP tools (`<5ms` offline response, zero npm dependencies): - `inspect_place({ year, place, lang? })`: Returns reigning monarch/era, controlling regime (`polity`), macro-region (`dao/lu/province`), prefecture (`jun/zhou/fu`), modern province/city, 2,400-year `lore`, and shareable deep-link URL. - `inspect_person({ person, stop?, lang? })`: Returns a historical figure or monarch's biography, chronological geocoded stops across dynasties, and shareable deep-link URL. - `search_atlas({ query, limit?, lang? })`: Searches across all ancient cities, poetic & battlefield landmarks, mountain passes, historical figures, imperial eras, and chronological milestones. - **Ready-to-Use Agent Skill**: [`skills/jiangshan-atlas/SKILL.md`](skills/jiangshan-atlas/SKILL.md) (includes the zero-dependency CLI renderer [`skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py`](skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py)) ```bash # Install into Claude Code / Gemini / Jetski global skills directory: mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills ~/.gemini/config/skills && cp -r skills/jiangshan-atlas ~/.claude/skills/ && cp -r skills/jiangshan-atlas ~/.gemini/config/skills/ ``` ### 1. Zero-Coordinate Dual-Parameter URL Protocol (0D Pinpoint / 1D Same-Year Route / 4D Multi-Year Route) | Mode | Example URL | Automatic Rendering Behavior | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Single-Point Pinpoint (0D)** | [`?year=819&place=蓝关&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=819&place=蓝关&lang=en)
*(Han Yu's 819 CE exile poem at Languan Pass)* | Jumps to Tang Yuanhe 14 (819 CE), drops a pin on Languan Pass in the Qinling Mountains, and opens its 2,400-year administrative genealogy card | | **Same-Year Multi-Stop Route (1D)** | [`?year=763&place=剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=763&place=剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳&lang=en)
*(Du Fu's 763 CE poem on recapturing Henan & Hebei)* | Plots numbered vermilion arcs `1` → `5` across the 763 CE Tang map and auto-fits the viewport; click any stop to inspect its genealogy | | **Multi-Year Space-Time Route (4D)** | [`?year=1079,1080,1094,1097&place=湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1079,1080,1094,1097&place=湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州&lang=en)
*(Su Shi's career across Huzhou, Huangzhou, Huizhou & Danzhou)* | Pairs `year[i]` with `place[i]`, labeling stops with their historical years and switching the underlying dynastic map whenever you click a stop | ### 2. CLI One-Command Screenshot & JSON Lookup (for Agent Tool Calls) ```bash # Single-point poetic landmark screenshot python3 skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py --year 819 --place 蓝关 --out /tmp/languan_819.png # Same-year multi-stop trajectory screenshot python3 skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py --year 763 --place 剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳 --out /tmp/dufu_763.png # Multi-year space-time trajectory screenshot python3 skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py --year 1079,1080,1094,1097 --place 湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州 --out /tmp/sushi_exile.png ``` ### 3. Browser JavaScript API (`window.atlasAPI`) & In-Browser WebMCP (`navigator.modelContext`) In browser automation environments (Playwright) or WebMCP-enabled AI browsers (`navigator.modelContext`), the page automatically registers `jiangshan_locate`, `jiangshan_inspect`, and `jiangshan_open_person`, and exposes `window.atlasAPI`: - `window.atlasAPI.locate({ year, place, zoom? })`: Drives the map to a single location or multi-stop trajectory and returns structured historical-geographic metadata. - `window.atlasAPI.inspect({ year, place, person?, stop? })`: Read-only query returning the controlling polity, ancient prefecture, modern province/city, leg distances, person events, and canonical shareable URL. - `window.atlasAPI.resolvePlace(place, year?)`: Resolves ancient and modern names for cities, strategic passes, poetic landmarks, and battlefields. - `window.atlasAPI.openPerson(person, stop?)` & `window.atlasAPI.search(query)`: Opens a person chronicle on the map or searches across the entire atlas. --- ## Run Locally No dependencies or build steps required. Clone and serve with any static HTTP server: ```bash git clone https://github.com/DeanChensj/jiangshan-map.git cd jiangshan-map python3 -m http.server 8000 ``` Then open `http://localhost:8000` in your browser. ## Run with Docker No local dependency needed. Build and start with Docker Compose: ```bash docker compose up -d --build ``` Then open `http://localhost:8008` (the port mapping `8008:80` is set in `docker-compose.yml`). The image is a plain `nginx:alpine` that serves this repository as static files: `Dockerfile` copies the working tree into `/usr/share/nginx/html`, and `.dockerignore` keeps the build context small by excluding `.git`, `.github`, `data/`, `docs/`, `scripts/`, `skills/`, Markdown files and `geojson/demo.html` — the site does not need any of them at runtime. To use another port, change the `ports` mapping in `docker-compose.yml` (e.g. `"9000:80"`) and run `docker compose up -d` again. After pulling upstream changes, rebuild with `docker compose up -d --build`. Without Compose: `docker build -t jiangshan-map:latest .` then `docker run -d -p 8008:80 --name jiangshan-map jiangshan-map:latest`. Note: the image is built locally; it is not published to any registry. --- ## GeoJSON Export (for Leaflet / MapLibre / QGIS) The app ships its geometry as compact topology-deduplicated VLQ bundles. To use the vector layers in other projects, generate standard RFC 7946 GeoJSON (EPSG:4326, lon/lat) locally; the output goes to `geojson/` and is not committed. The export covers 403 BCE to 1948; later years and the modern province layer are not included. ```bash node scripts/export_geojson.js # or: node scripts/export_geojson.js ``` - `snapshots/.geojson` — one file per territorial phase; each feature has a `bbox` and `layer` (`polity` / `region` / `prefecture`), `title`, `title_en`, `category`, `tint`, `anchor`. - `index.json` — every dynasty's phases with `from` / `to` years (negative = BCE, no year 0) and the matching snapshot file. - `corridors.geojson` (walls, canals, roads, sea routes), `settlements.geojson`, `milestones.geojson`, `neighbors.geojson`, and `modern/` (rivers, lakes, hydro labels; `appear` / `vanish` give the years historical river courses and lakes are shown). To look up a point without loading every phase, use [`geojson/jiangshan-locate.js`](geojson/jiangshan-locate.js): it loads `index.json` plus only the snapshot covering the year, then runs a bbox-filtered point-in-polygon test. ```js const atlas = JiangshanLocate.create(); // or create({ base: '' }) const hit = await atlas.locate(118.78, 32.06, 1415); // lon, lat, year hit.polity.properties.title; // 明 hit.region.properties.title; // 南直隶 hit.prefecture.properties.title; // 应天府 (a GeoJSON Feature: L.geoJSON(hit.prefecture)) ``` After exporting, serve the repository (`python3 -m http.server 8000`) and open `http://localhost:8000/geojson/demo.html` for a Leaflet example: drag the year slider, click the map, or open `demo.html?year=1415&lon=118.78&lat=32.06` to load, highlight and zoom automatically. Historical borders are schematic approximations, not surveyed boundaries. The data is GPL-3.0 except the prefecture-level boundaries noted under [Credits & License](#credits--license). --- ## Credits & License - **Historical GIS References**: Tan Qixiang's *The Historical Atlas of China* (谭其骧主编《中国历史地图集》), **CHGIS** (Harvard-Yenching Institute & Fudan University), **Robert M. Hartwell** historical GIS datasets, and [aourednik/historical-basemaps](https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps) (GPL-3.0). - **Modern Provincial Reference**: DataV GeoAtlas open administrative boundary data. - **Classical Guqin Audio**: Wikimedia Commons public-domain recordings (*Liu Shui*, *Pingsha Luoyan*, *Yangguan Sandie*, *Zuiyu Changwan*, *Jiu Kuang*). - **Approximate boundaries**: Historical territorial contours and administrative boundaries in this atlas are schematic approximations that illustrate broad historical jurisdictions. They are not the product of scientific surveying and should not be cited as precise or authoritative borders. - **Attribution**: When reusing maps, screenshots or data from this project, please credit **江山时序 Jiangshan Atlas** with a link to https://github.com/DeanChensj/jiangshan-map, and cite the upstream sources listed above. - **Contributing**: See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) ([中文贡献指南](CONTRIBUTING_ZH.md)) for repository structure, data conventions, and validation checks. - **License**: Released under **GPL-3.0** (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)). Copyright © 2026 DeanChensj. - **Exception**: Prefecture-level boundaries (commanderies, prefectures and superior prefectures, i.e. 郡 / 州 / 府, including the Warring States and Qin commanderies) derived from CHGIS V6 and the Hartwell China Historical GIS remain subject to their original terms (academic, non-commercial use only) and are not relicensed under GPL-3.0. See [data/atlas/README.md](data/atlas/README.md) for provenance and citation.

repositories.readme:
# herdr

herdr.dev · install · quick start · docs

English · 简体中文

--- https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/043ec09f-4bdd-41d5-aee0-8fda6b83e267 **the runtime your coding agents live on.** - **detach without stopping work** — herdr keeps terminals running in a background server when you close the client or lose your SSH connection. after a server or machine restart, herdr restores the saved layout and can resume supported agent sessions; the original processes do not survive. [session state →](https://herdr.dev/docs/session-state/) - **several machines, one window** — keep local work and saved ssh machines together, with a combined agent list and independent reconnects. [remote machines →](https://herdr.dev/docs/connecting-machines/) - **never hunt for the stuck one** — every pane is marked working, blocked, or idle. when an agent stops and needs an answer, herdr says so. - **agent-native** — agents drive herdr through the cli and socket api: they can spawn panes, prompt each other, and wait until another agent is genuinely blocked. [agent skill →](https://herdr.dev/docs/agent-skill/) - **runs what you already run** — claude code, codex, cursor, opencode, grok and the rest. herdr doesn't wrap or replace them; it owns their terminals. building an agent? [add herdr support →](https://herdr.dev/docs/add-herdr-support/) - **keyboard and mouse, both first-class** — tmux-style prefix keys *and* click, drag, split. pick per moment, not per tool. - **plugins** — extend panes and workflows. [browse the marketplace →](https://herdr.dev/plugins/) - **one rust binary, no electron** — runs in whatever terminal you already use. --- ## install ```bash curl -fsSL https://herdr.dev/install.sh | sh ``` or `brew install herdr` · `mise use -g herdr` · windows: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://herdr.dev/install.ps1 | iex"` · [endpoint-protected Windows](https://herdr.dev/docs/windows-beta/) · [binaries](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/releases) then start it where the work lives: ```bash herdr ``` run your agents, split panes, walk away. `ctrl+b q` detaches, `herdr` reattaches. [quick start →](https://herdr.dev/docs/quick-start/) ## docs everything lives at [herdr.dev/docs](https://herdr.dev/docs/): [quick start](https://herdr.dev/docs/quick-start/) · [concepts](https://herdr.dev/docs/concepts/) · [supported agents](https://herdr.dev/docs/agents/) · [keyboard](https://herdr.dev/docs/keyboard/) · [configuration](https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/) · [session state](https://herdr.dev/docs/session-state/) · [connecting machines](https://herdr.dev/docs/connecting-machines/) · [remote](https://herdr.dev/docs/persistence-remote/) · [integrations](https://herdr.dev/docs/integrations/) · [add herdr support to your agent](https://herdr.dev/docs/add-herdr-support/) · [plugins](https://herdr.dev/docs/plugins/) · [socket api](https://herdr.dev/docs/socket-api/) ## thanks every past sponsor and backer is listed in [SPONSORS.md](./SPONSORS.md) — thank you 🐑 enterprise / partnership: hey@herdr.dev ## agent instructions if you are an ai agent helping with this repository, read [`AGENTS.md`](./AGENTS.md) before making changes and read [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening issues or PRs. ## development ```bash git clone https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr cd herdr cargo build --release just test # unit tests just check # formatting, tests, and maintenance checks ``` ## license Herdr is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE).

# why many token when few do trick **Caveman make your AI agent say less and read less. Code stay exact. Brain still big.**

33.2% fewer

input tokens, whole sessions
54 Claude Code runs, 18 of 18 answers right

54% cheaper

with Auto, same score
85 coding tasks vs Opus 5.5 at xhigh, interim

397 → 76

tokens for one test run
Blocks vs | tail -20

1.4 to 2.4× cheaper

with caveman-style output
Adobe Research, eight models
Cited by **[Adobe Research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24083)** · A/B tested by **[JetBrains](https://blog.jetbrains.com/ai/2026/07/speak-to-ai-agents-like-cavemen-tosave-tokens/)** · Remade for Elasticsearch on **[Elasticsearch Labs](https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/elastic-caveman-ai-token-reduction)**
**#1** on [Hacker News](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47647455) · **#1** on GitHub Trending · *"No way this actually works."* [ThePrimeagen](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L29q2LRiMRc) **[Install](#install) · [Six rocks](#six-rocks-one-install) · [Proof](#proof) · [Say less](#say-less-the-caveman-voice) · [Read less](#read-less-332-fewer-input-tokens) · [Auto](#auto-54-cheaper-same-score) · [Blocks](#blocks-code-mode-script-written-once) · [Commands](#commands) · [Caveman Cloud](#caveman-cloud)**
---
Normal agent · 63 tokens Caveman agent · 20 tokens
> The reason your React component is re-rendering is likely because you're creating a new object reference on each render cycle. When you pass an inline object as a prop, React's shallow comparison sees it as a different object every time, which triggers a re-render. I'd recommend using useMemo to memoize the object. > New object ref each render, so React re-renders. Wrap the prop in `useMemo`.
**Same fix. 63 token become 20. Brain still big.** Pick your club: | Skill | Same answer | Tokens | |---|---|---:| | `/caveman` | New object ref each render, so React re-renders. Wrap the prop in `useMemo`. | 20 | | `/ultracave` | Inline object prop, new ref, re-render. `useMemo`. | 14 | | `/megacave` | 新參照致重繪。`useMemo`。 | **13** | Token counts: tiktoken o200k. ## Install ```bash npx @caveman-ai/cli@latest ``` One command. Mac, Linux, Windows. Caveman find your agents and your logins, show what it change. Press Enter. Done. Needs Node.js 22.13+. After that, plain `claude` stays caveman'd. So do Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and [30+ more](./INSTALL.md). It runs on your machine, with your keys and your Claude Pro/Max login. One rock. That it. Had caveman before 4.0? Say @latest, or the old copy on your machine wins. Already set up? caveman setup opens the screen again. Only want shorter answers? Get just the skill. ## Six rocks, one install New in 4.0: caveman is six parts. All on after install. Each has its own switch. | Rock | What it does | Measured | |---|---|---| | **[Say less](#say-less-the-caveman-voice)** | Agent answers short. Code stays exact | 63 → 20 tokens, same fix | | **[Read less](#read-less-332-fewer-input-tokens)** | Logs, JSON, CSV, test output shrink before the model reads them | **33.2%** fewer input tokens per session | | **[Auto](#auto-54-cheaper-same-score)** · new | Picks the model and the effort for each ask | **54%** cheaper than Opus at xhigh, same score | | **[Blocks](#blocks-code-mode-script-written-once)** · new | Code mode: agent keeps the scripts it writes and runs them again | **397 → 76** tokens for one test run | | **[Waste fixes](#smaller-rocks)** | Finds where your tokens go and fixes it. New: keeps the prompt cache warm while you pause | Not measured yet | | **[Browse](#smaller-rocks)** | Web pages come back compressed | **129.8×** smaller page | `caveman status` shows what is on. `caveman off browse` turns one off. Only Auto needs an account, and it is free. [4.0.0 release notes](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/releases/tag/v4.0.0) ## Proof Outside labs first. Ours come with each rock below. Nothing rounded up. Red rows stay red. | Who | Setup | Result | |---|---|---| | **[Adobe Research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24083)**, CAVEWOMAN paper (cites this repo) | Caveman-style output, eight models, five datasets | **Cost cut 1.4 to 2.4× per model, up to 3×** | | **[Elastic](https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/elastic-caveman-ai-token-reduction)**, Elasticsearch Labs | Caveman mode remade for Elasticsearch, eight live MCP scenarios | **63.6% fewer response tokens.** *"Zero information loss."* | | **[JetBrains](https://blog.jetbrains.com/ai/2026/07/speak-to-ai-agents-like-cavemen-tosave-tokens/)** | 86 real coding tasks, paired A/B | **No measurable quality loss** (p = 0.82). 8.5% fewer output tokens | Two findings shaped caveman. Adobe: cavemanning *your* prompt makes answers worse, so caveman never touches your prompt. JetBrains: agent sessions are mostly code and tool calls, which the voice leaves alone. So caveman grew rocks that shrink what the agent *reads* and what it *runs on*. ## Say less: the caveman voice **A voice, not broken grammar. Every reply follows the same structure.** | Rule | What it means | |---|---| | **Answer first** | `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].` No greeting, no "let me", no recap | | **One idea per sentence** | Built on [ASD-STE100](https://www.asd-ste100.org/), the controlled English of aircraft maintenance manuals: 20 words max, active voice, one term per thing | | **Meaning never dropped** | Articles can go. *not*, *never*, *no*, *only* never go. Numbers and units stay exact | | **Payload verbatim** | Code, commands, paths, and error messages untouched, character for character | | **No theater** | No "me think". No chatter between tool calls. If caveman phrasing isn't shorter, plain wins | | **Knows when to stop** | Security warnings, irreversible actions, and confused users get full sentences. Then grunt resumes | | **Your prompts stay yours** | Never rewritten. [Research say that backfire](#proof) | Ten dev questions on claude-opus-5-5: | Instruction | Output tokens | |---|---:| | None | 6,983 | | `Answer concisely.` | 4,334 | | `/caveman` | 4,119 | | `/ultracave` | **2,693** | "Be concise" is the real baseline; new models already know it. On top of it, `/caveman` cuts 3% more at the median and `/ultracave` 35% more. Measured on the 3.1.0 rules, not yet re-run. The rules cost about 1,160 tokens of input, and if you pay per request (GitHub Copilot), shorter answers save nothing. [Harness](./evals/README.md) · [Every case where caveman loses](./docs/HONEST-NUMBERS.md) **Only want this rock?** The skill alone, no proxy: ```bash npx skills add JuliusBrussee/caveman -g ``` Type `/caveman` (`$caveman` in Codex) if it doesn't start on its own. Say `stop caveman` to go back.
Other ways in: Claude app and phone, Claude Code plugin, Gemini, every agent at once, Windows, uninstall
Claude on the web, the phone app, or Cowork? No terminal. Add caveman to your Claude account once, in Customize > Plugins: [steps](./INSTALL.md#claude-apps-claudeai-desktop-mobile-cowork). Not tested end to end yet. ```bash # Claude Code plugin, auto-starts every interactive session, subagents too claude plugin marketplace add JuliusBrussee/caveman && claude plugin install caveman@caveman # Gemini CLI gemini extensions install https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman # Every agent on your machine at once, plus the Claude Code statusline badge (Node.js 22.13+) curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/v4.0.1/install.sh | bash ``` Already inside Claude Code? Same rock, slash form. Type these where you talk to Claude: ```text /plugin marketplace add JuliusBrussee/caveman /plugin install caveman@caveman ``` Windows, PowerShell 5.1+: ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/v4.0.1/install.ps1 | iex ``` On npm 12 or newer, new npm block git install. One-liners above handle it themselves from v3.2.0 on. Old one-liner pinned to v3.1.0 or older still fail there: use one above, or this: `npx --allow-git=root -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman#v4.0.1` Changed your mind: `npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman -- --uninstall` (on npm 12+, add `--allow-git=root` too) Only grabbed the skill? `npx skills remove JuliusBrussee/caveman -g` take it back out. Install broke? Open your agent in this repo and say *"Read CLAUDE.md and INSTALL.md, install caveman for me."* Agent fix own brain.
## Read less: 33.2% fewer input tokens **The voice shrinks what the agent says. This shrinks what it reads. Same answers: 18 of 18 right.** | File type | The file, through caveman | File saved | Whole Claude Code session, 3 runs | Session saved | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | CSV | 28,041 → **314** | **98.9%** | 165,823 → 74,484 | **55.1%** | | Logs | 22,810 → **348** | **98.5%** | 148,807 → 74,068 | **50.2%** | | YAML | 20,447 → **178** | **99.1%** | 132,124 → 71,027 | **46.2%** | | Test output | 18,806 → **203** | **98.9%** | 150,377 → 108,514 | **27.8%** | | JSON | 18,837 → **281** | **98.5%** | 147,975 → 108,939 | **26.4%** | | HTML | 21,670 → 21,670 | none yet | 140,687 → 154,641 | 9.9% worse | | **All six** | 130,611 → 22,994 | 82.4% | **885,793 → 591,673** | **33.2%** | *The file* is each test file through today's compressor alone. *The session* is the whole agent run, which also carries the system prompt and tools, so it moves less. Honest part: the session run is from August 2026 on an older engine, HTML has no compressor yet so it lost, and each test file hides one record in 61 to 72 KB of noise. Yours will vary. Headroom on the same suite: 15 of 18 right, 6.7% fewer tokens. [Method](./docs/WRAP-BENCHMARK.md#per-file-compression) Every original stays on your disk. The agent can pull it back any time. ## Auto: 54% cheaper, same score **New model in your agent's picker. Pick Auto and caveman chooses the model and the effort for each ask. Hard ask, big brain. Easy ask, save rocks.** | Setup | Tasks solved | Cost per try | Median time | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Opus 5.5, xhigh effort, every ask | 44.3% | $7.83 | 35.2 min | | **Auto**, Claude models only | **43.7%** | **$3.59** | **15.9 min** | | **Auto**, plus OpenAI and open models | 42.9% | $3.47 | 16.7 min | Auto costs 0.46× what Opus 5.5 at xhigh costs. That is 54% saved, in under half the time. 85 real coding tasks from SWE-Interact and SWE-Together, one try each. Honest part: the run is half done, the 0.5-point score gap is too small to tell apart at this size (±7), and most of the saving is Auto lowering effort on easy asks. Already on Opus at medium? Expect less; not measured yet. [Full table and limits](./docs/AUTO-BENCHMARK.md) ```bash caveman login # free account. Auto shows up in the model picker caveman providers add openai # optional: give Auto more models, on your own key ``` Works in Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex on a ChatGPT login, with API keys, Claude Pro/Max, or ChatGPT. Any other model you pick runs as picked. Not signed in: no Auto, nothing sent. [What Auto sends](#privacy) ## Blocks: code mode, script written once **skills.sh for code mode.** Code mode is the agent writing a script instead of making tool call after tool call ([Cloudflare](https://blog.cloudflare.com/code-mode/), [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp)). Problem: agent write same script every session, throw it away, write it again. Blocks keep it in your repo, check it every pull request, hand it back. | Input | Raw | What agents type now | Block | |---|---:|---:|---:| | `go test -v ./...`, 326 tests | 10,561 | 397 · `\| tail -20` | **76** · `test-summary` | | 1.4 MB JSON file | 251,893 | 236 · their own heredoc | **227** · `json-peek` | | 366-line Go file | 3,111 | **250** · `grep -n` | 489 · `grep-defs` | Tokens the agent reads back. In one week, agents on one machine wrote the same script [394 times](https://github.com/caveman-ai/blocks#one-script-written-394-times-in-a-week). [Purdue](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30725) measured the habit at up to 9.57% of task cost. `grep-defs` loses to a bare grep; row stays. [Method](https://github.com/caveman-ai/blocks#blocks-against-what-agents-type-now) Comes with caveman. Eight blocks ready: `json-peek` · `jsonl-stats` · `test-summary` · `first-error` · `wait-for` · `grep-defs` · `http-json` · `replace-in-file`. When the agent starts typing a script a block already covers, it gets one line: use the block. Never denies or rewrites a command. ```bash caveman-blocks scan # what your agents retyped this month. Script text never leaves your machine caveman-blocks init # rules and block index into this repo's AGENTS.md ``` Pre-release (v0.1.0-rc.5). Python only, no sandbox yet. Own repo, own stars: **[caveman-ai/blocks](https://github.com/caveman-ai/blocks)** ## Smaller rocks | Rock | What it does | Measured | |---|---|---| | `caveman learn` | Ranks where your tokens go, from agent history already on disk. `caveman learn implement` applies fixes one diff at a time, only on your yes | Not yet | | Warm cache · new | Step away and the provider forgets your session, so the next ask pays full price. Caveman keeps Anthropic's prompt cache warm while you pause, only when your own history says you come back in time. Every warm is listed in `caveman stats` | Not yet | | `caveman browse ` | A compressed web page for the agent | **121 tokens instead of 15,704** for a Playwright snapshot of a 200-row table. Tiny forms lose 2.3×. [Bench](./browse/BENCHMARK.md) | | `/caveman-compress ` | Shrinks memory files like `CLAUDE.md`, keeps a backup | **4,138 tokens instead of 6,198** across five files, 22.8% to 49.1% each, every heading, code block, and path intact. [Bench](./skills/caveman-compress/README.md#benchmarks) | | Middleware | Same shrinking inside the Vercel AI SDK, LangChain, OpenAI, or Anthropic call you already make. [TypeScript](./packages/middleware/typescript/README.md) · [Python](./packages/middleware/python/README.md) · [Every framework](https://docs.caveman.so/caveman/middleware) · [One container for the team](docs/technical/deploy.md) | Not yet |

## Commands In your terminal: ```bash caveman claude # start an agent on caveman: codex · gemini · opencode · aider · kilo · qwen · hermes · openclaw · pi caveman status # what is on, which agents it reaches, one next step caveman on browse # switch one rock on or off: output · input · waste-fixes · routing · scripts · browse caveman login # free account, turns on Auto caveman learn # where your tokens go caveman trial -- claude # A/B a real session on your own work caveman shrink -- pnpm test # compress noisy command output caveman convert --dry-run # pixel mode: skills the model reads as images caveman stats # your token history caveman doctor # one problem per line, with its fix ``` In your agent: | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `/caveman` · `/ultracave` · `/megacave` | The voice, the grunt, the 文言文. `/caveman status` shows the mode, `/caveman off` stops it | | `/caveman-commit` | One-line Conventional Commit | | `/caveman-review` | One finding per line: `L42: 🔴 null deref. Guard it.` | | `/caveman-compress ` | Shrinks memory files and backs up the original | | `/caveman-stats` | Real token usage for this Claude Code session | | `/caveman-help` | Every mode and command on one screen | | `cavecrew` | Subagents that find, edit, and review code, then report back in caveman | | `investigate-first` · `lean-build` · `surgical-patch` · `safe-refactor` · `migration` · `verify-and-stop` | Work patterns that write less code. Your agent picks them up when a task fits | | `caveman-setup` · `caveman-discover` · `caveman-learn` · `caveman-manage` · `caveman-optimize` · `caveman-explore` · `caveman-evidence-review` | Drive the proxy from inside your agent | ## Caveman Cloud **Everything above is for the coding agent you use. Caveman Cloud is for the agents you build.** You ship an agent. Every run costs money. Is it good? Is it cheap? Which change made it worse? Cloud answers. | Cloud does | What you get | |---|---| | **Observability** | Every run traced to the work and what it cost. Sets itself up from your repo, your keys, and the logs or OpenTelemetry you already have | | **Evals** | Grades how good the answers are, on your own tasks, from your real traffic | | **Autopilot** | Proposes a cheaper change, tests it on your recorded work, ships only when the evals say answers are still as good. You approve the pull request | | **Proof** | Every number says if it is measured, inferred, or verified. A saving counts only after real traffic shows it |

Sign up free  ·  Try the demo  ·  Book a call  ·  Docs

## In the wild **ThePrimeagen**: *"No way this actually works."* [Watch](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L29q2LRiMRc) **Adobe Research**: [CAVEWOMAN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24083), arXiv, June 2026 **JetBrains**: *"It is fun, and it costs you nothing measurable in quality."* [Read](https://blog.jetbrains.com/ai/2026/07/speak-to-ai-agents-like-cavemen-tosave-tokens/) **Elastic**: [elastic-caveman](https://www.elastic.co/search-labs/blog/elastic-caveman-ai-token-reduction) on Elasticsearch Labs, April 2026 **Hacker News**: [#1, 904 points](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47647455) **GitHub Trending** #1 overall, July 2026 · **[Trendshift](https://trendshift.io/repositories/25391)** #1 repo of the day, April 2026 · **[Product Hunt](https://www.producthunt.com/products/caveman)** #8 of the day Started as a joke in April 2026. Now past 100,000 stars. Joke got serious. Voice did not.
[![Star History Chart](./docs/assets/star-history.png)](https://star-history.com/#JuliusBrussee/caveman&Date) ## Privacy - **The skill** runs on your machine and sends nothing. One exception: `/caveman-compress` sends the file you compress to your configured model provider. - **The CLI** sends usage stats by default: commands run, token counts, caveman-blocks commands and usage counts, a random install ID, OS, and IP. Never your prompts, code, file paths, or scripts you wrote. One person maintains this for free, and those stats show what to build next. Off for good, Blocks included: `caveman telemetry off` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`. - **Auto**, only once you sign in and pick it: each ask sends Caveman Cloud your latest ask (with whatever your agent attaches to it, such as CLAUDE.md, memory or @-mentioned files), the one before it, and the end of the agent's last reply, plus each request's tool names, effort, a few agent headers, and the previous request's token counts. On the Free plan Caveman may keep it to improve routing. `caveman off routing` stops it. - **Where requests go:** from your machine to your provider, or to another provider you added with `caveman providers add`, on your own key. Only a request routed to a Caveman Cloud model passes through Caveman Cloud, whole (system prompt, tool results, code), on your Caveman project's stored key, billed to that project. `caveman providers cloud off` stops that. The full list, and how to delete sent telemetry: [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md). ## License [Apache-2.0](./LICENSE), whole repo. Read it, fork it, ship it, host it. Free like mammoth on open plain. Older releases and third-party notices: [LICENSING.md](./LICENSING.md). "Caveman" and the rock logo are trademarks of Julius Brussee. ## Cite ```bibtex @software{brussee2026caveman, author = {Brussee, Julius}, title = {Caveman: why many token when few do trick}, year = {2026}, url = {https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman} } ``` ---
🪨 **Caveman save you token. Star cost zero. Fair trade.** Docs · Install matrix · Honest numbers · Contributing · Caveman Cloud · Issues
